questions.q: $\mathbf{v}$ lies along an eigenvector with $\lambda = -1.8$ and $\|\mathbf{v}\| = 2$. What is $A\mathbf{v}$?
options: An arrow of length $3.6$ pointing the same way
An arrow of length $1.8$ pointing the opposite way
An arrow of length $3.6$ pointing the opposite way
questions.explain: $\|A\mathbf{v}\| / \|\mathbf{v}\| = |\lambda| = 1.8$, so the length becomes $3.6$; the negative sign flips the direction. 'Flip + Grow': a negative $\lambda$ does not mean shrinking.

questions.q: Which eigenvalue makes its eigen-direction **shrink** toward the origin *without* flipping?
questions.explain: $0 < \lambda < 1$ shrinks while keeping the direction. $-0.4$ also shrinks but flips; $2$ grows; $1$ leaves the vector unchanged.

questions.q: In the 2D Matrix View you set $A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0.5 \end{bmatrix}$. What does the unit circle become?
options: An axis-aligned ellipse with semi-axes $3$ (horizontal) and $0.5$ (vertical)
questions.explain: For a diagonal matrix the eigenvalues sit on the diagonal and the eigen-directions are the axes, so the semi-axes (half-width, half-height) are exactly $|\lambda_1| = 3$ and $|\lambda_2| = 0.5$. $1.5$ and $0.25$ confuse semi-axes with half of them.

questions.q: A simple RNN applies the same recurrent matrix 10 times. Along an eigen-direction with $\lambda = 0.9$, how large is the signal after 10 steps (starting from 1)?
questions.explain: Each step multiplies by $0.9$: $0.9^{10} \approx 0.349$. $|\lambda| < 1$ causes vanishing, while $1.1^{10} \approx 2.59$ would show exploding. $9 = 10 \times 0.9$ adds instead of compounding.
